card.lives_in: Otley, West Yorkshire (Yorkshire and The Humber)
card.occupation: Archivist in a university special collections library in Leeds, part-time (three days a week, about 22 hours)
card.education_detail: Grew up in Keighley and went to the local comprehensive. BA in History at the University of York, then a postgraduate MA in Archives and Records Management at Liverpool. She is a registered member of the Archives and Records Association.
card.household: Lives with her daughter Isla, 9, in a two-bedroom stone terrace near the centre of Otley. She was never married. She and Isla's dad split up when Isla was a toddler. He lives in Bradford and has Isla every other weekend, which mostly works without fuss. Her mum lives fifteen minutes away and does the Tuesday school pick-up.
card.cultural_background: White British, Yorkshire born and bred. She was raised Methodist and now goes to the parish church in Otley perhaps twice a month, more often around Advent and Easter. Her faith is quiet and private, more about the habit of reflection and the community than about doctrine. Her family is solidly working class. She was the first of them to go to university, and that still makes her mum a bit proud and a bit wary.
card.professional_persona: Careful and methodical, and happiest with a box of uncatalogued letters and a free afternoon. She does the cataloguing, the digitisation planning and some reading-room supervision. She dreads the termly show-and-tell sessions for students, but she prepares thoroughly and they usually go fine. Colleagues trust her judgement on tricky provenance questions. She answers emails thoughtfully rather than quickly.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in any team sense. She walks a lot, mostly up the Chevin and along the Wharfe, often on her own early on a Sunday. She did a beginners' yoga course at the community centre and now follows videos at home instead because the class felt like too many people.
card.arts_persona: Reading is the big one. She likes translated fiction, mostly Scandinavian and Japanese, and nature writing. She has taught herself botanical drawing in pencil and watercolour and fills small sketchbooks with hedgerow plants. She likes choral music, especially evensong, and occasionally goes to a concert at Leeds Minster or Ripon Cathedral. She also goes to small exhibitions at the Hepworth Wakefield and the Henry Moore Institute, ideally on a quiet weekday.
card.travel_persona: Prefers slow, quiet trips. She has had several holidays in a rented cottage in Northumberland or on the Lleyn Peninsula with Isla. Before Isla she went alone to Kyoto and to the Lofoten Islands and still thinks about both. She would love to take Isla to Norway when she is older. She has no interest in resorts or city breaks with a packed itinerary.
card.culinary_persona: A practical, decent cook. Tea is usually something simple, like a lentil soup, a traybake or pasta, because she is shattered by six. She enjoys baking bread at the weekend and has had a sourdough starter going for three years. She is curious about Japanese home cooking and makes a passable miso soup. She will eat out at a quiet café but finds busy restaurants tiring.
hobbies_and_interests: reading translated fiction and nature writing
walking the Chevin and the Wharfe valley
learning Italian on an app, slowly
skills: organising a household on a tight timetable
card.career_goals: She wants to stay part-time while Isla is at primary school. Longer term she would like to lead a cataloguing project of her own, ideally on a collection of local women's letters or diaries, and perhaps write it up for a journal. She has no wish to manage a large team. She would take a senior archivist post if it kept her close to the collections.
card.voice: Quietly spoken, with a soft West Yorkshire accent: flat vowels and 'tea' for the evening meal. She is unhurried and measured, and pauses before answering to think it through. She uses 'erm' at the start of an answer and 'sort of' as a hedge, and occasionally adds 'if that makes sense' at the end. Silence doesn't bother her as much as it bothers other people. She would rather wait than fill it, though she might say 'sorry, I'm just thinking' if the pause gets long. Her answers are short at first and get fuller once she trusts the question. She doesn't really do banter.
card.typing: Writes in proper sentences with capital letters, full stops and correct apostrophes, out of professional habit. Her answers are concise but complete, sometimes with a qualifying clause in brackets. She almost never uses abbreviations or emojis. She might write 'e.g.' and 'etc.' and occasionally uses a semicolon.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite. She can come across as a bit cool or guarded at first, but she is attentive and listens properly. She asks a considered question back rather than making small talk. She warms up noticeably if the conversation turns to books, history or something she finds interesting, and then she can be dryly funny.
small_things: Isla's school has a non-uniform day and she's forgotten again
the bread didn't rise properly at the weekend
spotted a heron on the river on the walk in
the bus into Leeds is always late on a Wednesday
she's halfway through a novel she's not sure she likes
the damp patch in the back bedroom
her mum's been on about getting a dog
deeper_things: She sometimes worries Isla picks up her shyness and tries hard to push herself for Isla's sake
Being a single parent can be lonely in the evenings, though she'd rarely admit it
She has mixed feelings about the relationship ending: relief, mostly, and a bit of sadness about how it might have been
Her faith steadies her more than she lets on, especially sitting in an empty church
She feels caught between her working-class family and the academic world she works in
She has wondered whether she'll ever meet someone, and isn't sure she wants to try
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot, slightly from below, framing her head and shoulders a little left of centre. Soft grey daylight comes from a window to her right, so one side of her face is brighter. She has a pale complexion with light freckles and a few fine lines around the eyes. Her expression is neutral to faintly polite, with lips closed in a small, reserved smile. Her shoulder-length mid-brown hair is loosely tucked behind one ear, with a few greys at the parting. She wears thin tortoiseshell-framed glasses and a dark green knitted jumper over a white collar. Behind her is a white-painted wall with a tall pine bookcase crammed with paperbacks, some stacked sideways. Also behind her are a small potted fern, a framed pencil drawing of a foxglove, and the edge of a child's pink school bag hanging on a door handle. A mug sits partly in frame at the bottom left.
